author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected
summary: A booked visit can be corrected after booking: its date and its description can both be changed. The correction replaces that visit rather than adding a second one, and it is held to the same rules as the original booking.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is begun, then that visit's current date and description are offered for editing
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new details
given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet has no more visits than before, and the owner's record is shown
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the details are offered again
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the details are offered again
given a visit that does not belong to the named pet, when its correction is attempted, then it is refused (Visits edge case 3)
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit, and deleting one (NG-4, NG-5)
moving a visit to a different pet or owner
any link or button pointing to correction from the owner's record
notes: Owner-stated interface constraints for this slice (address, form reuse, model attribute) are recorded verbatim in the intake-decision at handoff line 1; they are mechanism, and the design stage owns them. Two open questions recorded in docs/prd.md rather than blocked on, per the intake's no-further-answer instruction: whether a visible entry point follows, and whether refusing another pet's visit is intended (taken as refused, extending Visits edge case 1). The docs/adr/README.md index row for adr/2026-09-08-non-goal-visit-correction.md is unwritten - that file is outside product-requirements-expert write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction is the existing create-or-update controller pair applied to visits. PetController already demonstrates the whole shape in the same package: an @ModelAttribute loader taking an optional path variable, a GET that returns the shared form view, and a POST that mutates the loaded aggregate member in place and saves through OwnerRepository. VisitController's loadPetWithVisit gains the same optional-visitId branch; on the edit path it resolves the visit from owner.getPet(petId).getVisits() and returns it as the visit model attribute without calling pet.addVisit, which is exactly what keeps the pet's visit count unchanged. Form binding then mutates that persisted Visit in place and owners.save(owner) persists it by the cascade already recorded in system-design.md Contracts (Invariants the rows cannot carry) and Persistence. No new type, package, repository, or pattern; the adjustment is one conditional in the loader plus a second handler pair. The template and its visit model attribute are reused unchanged, per the owner's interface constraint at handoff line 1.
integration_points: Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): keep the suite's existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository. It is a Spring Data JpaRepository interface, so no hand-written double is practical and the @WebMvcTest slice loads no persistence layer. The stub returns a real Owner-Pet-Visit graph the test builds; the controller mutates that graph in place, so the assertions on new date, new description, and unchanged visit count run against real domain objects rather than captured mock arguments.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the project's one sanctioned mock, drives the real dispatch, binding, and validation machinery for both the GET prefill and the POST outcomes.
No third boundary is crossed: no external service, no filesystem, no clock abstraction beyond LocalDate.now() already used by the booking path.

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute loader with @PathVariable(name=..., required=false); null means create, present means resolve through the owner graph. The visitId branch mirrors this exactly.
GET /edit returning the shared form view plus POST /edit mutating the existing aggregate member and saving through OwnerRepository, then redirecting to the owner detail page.

Existing booking handler: manual non-future-date rejection, result.hasErrors() redisplay of pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, RedirectAttributes flash message, redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. The correction handler follows this shape.

risks.risk: The correction repeats the non-future-visit-date rule, and architecture-principles.md pattern catalog (Web controller row) plus its checklist state that a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the existing deviation.
risks.mitigation: Introduce no new rule: express the existing non-future-date check once as a private helper on VisitController and call it from both handlers. Do not move the rule to a bean-validation constraint or a Validator in this slice; that reshapes REQ-VIS-001's error code and is out of scope.

risks.risk: The edit path adding a second visit instead of correcting the booked one, if the loader keeps calling pet.addVisit unconditionally.
risks.mitigation: On the edit branch return the resolved persisted Visit without attaching it (architecture-principles.md, Aggregate row: outside code enters through the root and the root owns its children). The acceptance criterion asserting the pet's visit count is unchanged is the test that pins this.

risks.risk: Identifier tampering on the new visitId path variable: a caller submitting a visit that belongs to another pet or another owner.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by walking owner to pet to visits, matching on identity, and reject a non-match the way the loader already rejects an unknown owner or pet (security-principles.md Trust Boundaries, External input arrives; system-design.md Contracts, Invariants the rows cannot carry). No global visit lookup exists and none is introduced.

risks.risk: Mass assignment through the new endpoint.
risks.mitigation: The controller-wide @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id already covers every handler in VisitController (security-principles.md Realization, Mass assignment row). Leave it controller-wide rather than narrowing it to one attribute name.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. Design-doc writes this dispatch: system-design.md Contracts rows for VisitController, Visit, and OwnerRepository now cite REQ-VIS-003 (contracts-sync), the VisitController purpose line names correction, and the invariants paragraph gained one sentence stating that a pet and a visit are resolved by walking the owner graph rather than by a global lookup. docs/adr/README.md gained the index row for 2026-09-08-non-goal-visit-correction.md, which the prd-entry flagged as outside the product expert's write scope. No new ADR: the product decision is already recorded in that non-goal ADR, and the mechanism follows the recorded feature-package and JPA-cascade decisions with no fresh trade-off. Narrowest-reading calls taken per the intake's no-further-answer instruction, each with the open question recorded rather than blocked on. First, the template is reused with no edit, so two cosmetic artifacts follow: the submit button keeps the addVisit message key, and the Previous Visits table lists the visit being corrected, because its th:if filter only hides unpersisted visits. Changing either touches REQ-VIS-001 and REQ-VIS-002 surfaces and was not requested; if the follow-up request adds a visible entry point, revisit both then. Second, refusal of another pet's visit takes the loader's existing IllegalArgumentException shape, matching how an unknown owner or pet is already refused, rather than introducing a new error surface.

findings.description: The private helper `findVisit` carries a full Javadoc block with @param and @return tags. The project's own convention (checklist default: 'public types and API only, one sentence of purpose') and the sibling private helpers in PetController (updatePetDetails, isDuplicatePetNameViolation) carry no Javadoc at all. The @return tag ('Returns the pet's own visit with that identifier') largely restates the signature. This is a placement/scope overreach, not a wrong idea — the WHY content (visit resolved only by walking the pet's own list, refusing a foreign visit id) is worth keeping but belongs in a short `//` comment, matching the style already used just above on processUpdateVisitForm (line 126-127), not a Javadoc block with tags.
findings.fix: Replace the /** ... */ Javadoc on findVisit with a brief `//` comment stating only the WHY (no global visit lookup exists; a visit is reached only by walking this owner's pet, which is what refuses a foreign visit id), dropping the @param/@return tags.

findVisit resolves the visit only by walking owner -> pet -> visits and rejects a mismatch via the existing IllegalArgumentException shape, consistent with how loadPetWithVisit already refuses an unknown owner or pet — no new error surface, no global visit lookup introduced (IDOR risk mitigated as designed).

New VIEWS_VISITS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM constant and initUpdateVisitForm/processUpdateVisitForm naming match the existing per-file convention (VisitController already names its new-visit handlers initNewVisitForm/processNewVisitForm) and the sibling VIEWS_PETS_.../VIEWS_OWNER_... constants in PetController/OwnerController.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: processUpdateVisitForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and calls owners.save(owner), so a crafted POST to the correction URL can bind non-identifier owner and nested pet fields (for example firstName, or pets[0].name) and persist them through the aggregate save. Identifier binding is blocked, and this is the same pattern processNewVisitForm already uses upstream, so the change is not weaker than the recorded baseline in an application with no authentication - noted for awareness, not as a defect of this slice. Narrowing the bound fields would have to be done for both handlers together if it is ever done.

No test locks the disallowed-field binder on the new correction path. A test posting id=<other visit id> to the correction URL and asserting the corrected visit is still the path-named one would pin the mass-assignment control against a future binder edit.

Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle is unchanged in the change set (no dependency delta), and the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured, so dependencyCheckAnalyze could not run. Resolved framework versions were not matched against CVE data here - a CI or human check closes that gap.
approved_aspects: IDOR / trust boundary: visitId is resolved only by walking owner -> pet -> pet.getVisits() in VisitController.findVisit; there is no repository lookup of a visit by id, so a visit id belonging to another pet or another owner cannot be reached. The refusal is regression-tested (VisitControllerTests.theCorrectionOfAnotherPetsVisitShouldBeRefused).

Cross-request state: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner, pet, and visit on every request including the POST, so the correction handler trusts no identifier validated by an earlier request (security-principles.md, 'Trusting cross-request state').

Mass assignment: VisitController's @InitBinder setAllowedFields disallows 'id' and '*.id' and applies to both the visit and owner binders, so a submitted id cannot re-point the corrected entity. Consistent with OwnerController and PetController (security-principles.md, 'Mass assignment').

Output escaping: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged and renders visit date and description through th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping; no th:utext, no inline script, no request-derived value in a template expression.

Error surface: the new IllegalArgumentException message carries only the path-bound integers visitId and petId. The error page renders exception messages (a recorded baseline defect), but this message leaks no sensitive value, and the failure mode matches the existing pet-not-found path.
Exposed surface: the two added routes are nested under the existing owner/pet path, are documented in the PRD and system-design contracts table, and add no management-endpoint exposure.
No injection surface added: no string-concatenated query, no shell or process execution, no file or path handling, no deserialization, no logging, and no new dependency.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Contained to one module: VisitController and its test plus five prose docs, 57 prod lines over 33 hunks, no sensitive paths. The only shared surface touched is the loadPetWithVisit model-attribute loader, and its new visitId path variable is optional with the original null branch preserved verbatim, so the booking path is unchanged and its existing tests stay green.

semantic_surprise.note: Refusing a foreign visit id is implemented as an unhandled IllegalArgumentException from findVisit, so a hand-edited URL on the new public route lands on the error page the PRD itself records as a defect for showing technical detail (REQ-SYS-002). The requirement says only that the correction is refused, and the test asserts the exception rather than an HTTP status, so the user-visible shape of that refusal is a choice the diff does not announce. Two other candidates read clean: binding mutates the persisted Visit in place before validation, but spring.jpa.open-in-view=false leaves it detached so a refused correction never flushes, and Pet.visits is a LinkedHashSet over identity-hashed BaseEntity so mutating a member's date cannot corrupt the set.

test_adequacy.note: The six new tests assert real outcomes on the real mutated domain graph rather than on mock interactions: the corrected date and description are read back off the bookedVisit instance, the no-extra-visit invariant is a before-and-after size check on the pet's visits, and the two refusal cases are a parameterized test asserting the named field error. They would fail against a broken implementation. The one gap is the security reviewer's: no test pins the disallowed-field binder on the new correction URL.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved with empty findings, but the security reviewer's approval carries three recommendations rather than none, and two are live residuals rather than polish: processUpdateVisitForm binds the Owner model attribute and calls owners.save(owner), so a crafted POST to the correction URL can bind non-identifier owner and nested pet fields through the aggregate save, and no test locks that control on the new path. Both are inherited from the booking handler and neither is a defect of this slice, but the correction route widens where the pattern is reachable.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions. The diff matches the recorded intake exactly: two routes under the existing owner-pet path, the createOrUpdateVisitForm template and its visit model attribute reused unchanged, and no edit link added to the owner page, which the PRD states outright. The NG-5 narrowing is recorded as its own non-goal ADR in the convention the earlier ADR prescribed. Extracting the view-name constant and rejectVisitDateNotInFuture touches the existing booking handler, but both are behavior-preserving and the design block named the rule reuse.

rationale: Correct and contained, but read two things before merging: the foreign-visit-id refusal exits through the error page the PRD records as a defect, and the correction POST saves the whole Owner aggregate with request-bound owner fields, unpinned by any test. Both are inherited patterns; the new public route widens their reach.
